text:
maya: thinking out loud — we should land on a compact span-name + rich attributes approach for LLM requests. current proposals are all over the place and exporters are getting noisy :grimacing:

devin: +1. my vote: keep span.name generic and use semantic attrs for everything LLM-specific. e.g. span.name = "llm.request" or "llm.inference"; attrs carry model, seq lengths, cache flags, route. easier to group in traces and dashboards.

sasha: curious how this interacts with routing policies — we often need to filter traces by routing decision (priority vs best-effort). should that be an attribute or a separate span?

maya: attribute. simple string like routing.policy = "latency" / "cost" / "dedicated". that keeps trace graph simpler.

raj: thinking about retention/export: we don't want full token streams in traces (PII + size). we should only export token counts and cache-hit booleans. full prompts go to secure logs if needed for eval, gated by access.

devin: agreed. propose attr set: model.family, model.variant, model.size, tokens.prompt_count, tokens.completion_count, kvcache.hit (bool), kvcache.prefix_len, routing.policy, region, customer_tier. no raw text fields.

maya: I threw together an example OTEL attr payload for the runtime team:

```
span.name: "llm.request"
span.kind: client
attributes:
  service.name: "redwood.inference"
  telemetry.source: "runtime"
  model.family: "llama3"
  model.variant: "llama3-13B-quant"
  model.size: "13B"
  model.revision: "r2"
  tokens.prompt_count: 42
  tokens.completion_count: 128
  tokens.total: 170
  kvcache.hit: true
  kvcache.hit_ratio: 0.84
  routing.policy: "latency"
  route.fallback: "gpt-compat-7b"
  region: "us-west-2"
  customer_tier: "enterprise"
  request.id: "req_9a2b3c"
```

sasha: love it. two nitpicks: 1) use snake_case for attrs? we have mixed casing across services. 2) consider adding sampling.hint or telemetry.sensitive: true/false so exporters can decide to drop sensitive attrs.

devin: for consistency we should standardize on dot.delimited keys for model.* and snake_case for generic metrics like tokens_count. mixing will break queries. proposal: dot keys for domain (model.family) and snake for counters (tokens_prompt).

maya: that's reasonable. add telemetry.sensitivity_level: "low|medium|high". runtime sets it to high when prompt contains user-submitted personal data; exporters drop high-level traces unless flagged for secured retention.

raj: exporter side: implement two export pipelines — default (90d retention, scrubbed attrs, no prompt text) -> standard traces backend; secure (365d retention, restricted access) -> compliant archive. sampling: keep 1% long term, 100% short window for debugging.

otel-bot: span-export-rule: matched(resource.service.name=="redwood.inference" && attributes.telemetry.sensitivity_level!="high") -> send: standard-traces, retention:90d
otel-bot: span-export-rule: matched(resource.service.name=="redwood.inference" && attributes.telemetry.sensitivity_level=="high") -> send: secure-archive, retention:365d, access:restricted

devin: question — dashboards. If span.name is generic, how do SRE and product find model-specific error rates? We need a canonical label that Grafana/ES queries can pivot on.

maya: docs/devex should publish canonical attribute keys. dashboards should use model.family + model.variant filters. also create a derived metric exporter that aggregates per-model QPS, p50/p95 latency, cache_hit_rate. metrics live in metrics backend (not traces) so queries are fast.

raj: derived metrics: make sure we record tokens-per-request and cost-estimate attribute so billing and cost dashboards align. exporters can emit a metric tokens.emitted with value tokens.total and tag model.family.

sasha: small UX note for rollouts: when we do canary of a new variant, the console should show traces/time-series split by model.revision so product can compare latency and quality. requires consistent labeling.

maya: action items:
- runtime team: adopt span.name = "llm.request" and implement attribute set (maya's example) with dot-keys for domain and snake_case counters. (owner: @devin)
- eng-telemetry: implement sensitivity-level tagging and exporter rules (owner: @raj)
- devex: write canonical keys doc + dashboard templates (owner: @sasha)
- security: confirm retention / secure-archive gating (owner: @maria)

devin: I'll open RFC PR with samples and a small test harness to assert exporters drop high-sensitivity traces.

sasha: can you also add a short example of span naming for multi-step ops (e.g., retrieval -> generate -> rerank)? suggestion: keep base name and add step attr step="retrieve|generate|rerank" rather than multiple span names.

maya: +1. step attr is clean and lets traces show timeline.

raj: last thought — KV cache metrics: we should avoid exposing exact cache keys; only expose hit/miss ratios and prefix length.

maya: agreed. thanks everyone. I'll draft the PR and ping reviewers. :thumbsup:

devin: thanks — will review today.

otel-bot: deploy-check: telemetry-rules-lint passed on branch "llm-trace-attrs"

maya: merging this week unless there are objections.
